reading_note: The teaching unfolds the anatomy of the sensual proprium: the "dragon" is the enthumesis of the body — that affection which lives wholly from sense impressions and corporeal appetite. Its "seven heads" are the external senses on the upper register (sight, hearing, smell, taste, plus the discriminating faculty), through which falsity enters and natural images are gathered. Its "five caves" are the lower bodily passages — throat, breath, generative and digestive openings — through which the same self-love expresses itself outward. Together upper and lower form a complete circuit of merely natural reception. The arc moves from diagnosis (mapping the sensual affection's organs) to combat: the spiritual man, recognizing this dragon as the body's own enthumesis, wars against it from above and below and prevails. This is what "Virgin" (uncorrupted reception) and "Continent" (restraint from sensual influx) genuinely mean.
